title: Fixed #35044 -- Avoided clearing reverse relations and private fields when accessing deferred fields.
evidence:
Fix message says: Fixed #35950 -- Restored refreshing of relations when fields deferred.

Thank you to Simon Charette and Sarah Boyce for the review.

Regression in 73df8b54a2fab53bec4c7573cda5ad8c869c2fd8.
reason: The change adds the `fields is None or field.name in fields` guards in `refresh_from_db`. Those guards misfire when `fields` has been reassigned internally for deferred instances, so a plain `refresh_from_db()` no longer clears cached reverse and private relations; the fix attributes this regression to this change.
ground_truth: In `Model.refresh_from_db()`, the change makes clearing of cached reverse relations (`_meta.related_objects`) and cached private relations (`_meta.private_fields`, e.g. GenericForeignKey) conditional on `fields is None or field.name in fields`. However, when `refresh_from_db()` is called without `fields` on an instance that has deferred fields, the method's existing code reassigns the local `fields` to the set of non-deferred concrete field attnames. That set never contains reverse-relation or private-field names, so the new condition is always false and these caches are never cleared. For example, loading `Secondary.objects.defer("first").get(...)`, accessing the reverse one-to-one `obj.primary_o2o` (now cached), then calling `obj.refresh_from_db()` leaves the stale related object in place instead of reloading it. A plain full refresh is supposed to clear all relation caches. The fix stops overwriting `fields` and passes the computed attname set directly to `.only()`, so `fields` stays None and all cached relations are cleared again.

title: Fixed #34060 -- Fixed migrations crash when adding check constraints with JSONField __exact lookup on Oracle.
evidence:
Fix message says: Refs #34060 -- Fixed JSONField __exact lookup for primitivies on Oracle 21c+.

Regression in c991602ce5798385261381025c06698d7fd30dc5.

Co-Authored-By: Mariusz Felisiak <felisiak.mariusz@gmail.com>
reason: The fix explicitly names this change as the regression. The faulty `JSONExact.as_oracle` method is added in this diff, and it returns wrong query results on Oracle 21c+.
ground_truth: The change adds `JSONExact.as_oracle`, which compiles a JSONField `__exact` lookup on Oracle to a bare `JSON_EQUAL(lhs, rhs)`. On Oracle 21c+ (`supports_primitives_in_json_field`), JSON values can be scalar primitives such as strings, numbers or booleans. Without the `JSON()` constructor, `JSON_EQUAL` does not handle such scalar operands. Its default FALSE ON ERROR behaviour then makes the comparison silently evaluate to false instead of raising. As a result, queries like `JSONModel.objects.filter(value="foo")`, `filter(value=True)`, or key transforms that compare against a primitive return no rows even when matching data exists. The fix wraps both operands in `JSON(...)` when the backend supports primitives and adds `ERROR ON ERROR` to the `JSON_EQUAL` call.

title: Fixed #35270 -- Optimized model's Options._property_names.
evidence:
Fix message says: Fixed #35301 -- Fixed Options._property_names for overriden properties.

Regression in faeb92ea13f0c1b2cc83f45b512f2c41cfb4f02d.
reason: The new MRO walk in `_property_names` collects a name if any ancestor class defines it as a property, even when a subclass overrides that name with a non-property. That is a behavioral regression introduced directly in this diff.
ground_truth: The rewritten `Options._property_names` iterates over `self.model.__mro__` and adds every name whose value in some `klass.__dict__` is a `property`. It does not check whether a class earlier in the MRO already shadows that name with a non-property attribute. Example: an abstract parent model defines `foo` as a `@property` and a child model overrides `foo` with a plain attribute or a field. `foo` is still reported in the child's `_property_names`. Code that relies on this set then treats the name as a property and mishandles it, for example `Model.__init__`/`_prepare_related_fields` kwargs handling and `QuerySet` create/update_or_create validation. The old `inspect.getattr_static` version resolved the attribute as normal lookup would. The fix tracks names already seen in earlier MRO classes and only counts a property if its name was not defined in a more-derived class.

title: Fixed #35537 -- Changed EmailMessage.attachments and EmailMultiAlternatives.alternatives to use namedtuples.
evidence:
Fix message says: Fixed #36309 -- Made email alternatives and attachments pickleable.

Regression in aba0e541caaa086f183197eaaca0ac20a730bbe4 and in
d5bebc1c26d4c0ec9eaa057aefc5b38649c0ba3b.

Thanks Florent Messa for the report, and Jake Howard and Claude
Paroz for the review.
reason: The change assigns a namedtuple whose type name differs from its module variable (`EmailAttachment = namedtuple("Attachment", ...)`), so attachments cannot be pickled. The fix explicitly names this commit as a regression source.
ground_truth: The change adds the module-level `EmailAttachment = namedtuple("Attachment", ["filename", "content", "mimetype"])` in `django/core/mail/message.py`. `EmailMessage.attach()` now stores each attachment as an instance of it. Pickle serializes namedtuple instances by looking up the class by its `__qualname__` ("Attachment") in its module. No `Attachment` attribute exists in `django.core.mail.message`; the class is bound to the name `EmailAttachment`. As a result, pickling an `EmailMessage` with any attachment fails with a `PicklingError` (attribute lookup Attachment on django.core.mail.message failed), e.g. `msg.attach("a.txt", "x", "text/plain"); pickle.dumps(msg)`, which breaks queuing emails through task queues or caches. The fix renames the namedtuple type names to match their variable names (`namedtuple("EmailAttachment", ...)`, and likewise `EmailAlternative`).

title: Fixed CVE-2024-39614 -- Mitigated potential DoS in get_supported_language_variant().
evidence:
Fix message says: Fixed #35627 -- Raised a LookupError rather than an unhandled ValueError in get_supported_language_variant().

LocaleMiddleware didn't handle the ValueError raised by
get_supported_language_variant() when language codes were
over 500 characters.

Regression in 9e9792228a6bb5d6402a5d645bc3be4cf364aefb.
reason: The change added a ValueError raise in get_supported_language_variant(). Callers such as LocaleMiddleware and get_language_from_path only catch LookupError, so overly long language codes cause unhandled exceptions (HTTP 500). The fix explicitly blames this change.
ground_truth: The security patch added a length check to `get_supported_language_variant()`. When `lang_code` exceeds `LANGUAGE_CODE_MAX_LENGTH` (500) and no generic variant can be cut off (or `strict=True`), it raises `ValueError("'lang_code' exceeds the maximum accepted length")`. This breaks the function's documented contract of raising `LookupError` when nothing is found. Callers like `LocaleMiddleware` and `get_language_from_path()`/`get_language_from_request()` only catch `LookupError`, and they call it with strict=True for URL path prefixes and cookies. So a request whose URL language prefix or language cookie is longer than 500 characters crashes with an unhandled ValueError (HTTP 500) instead of falling back to another language. Fixed by raising `LookupError(lang_code)` instead of ValueError.

title: Fixed #35331 -- Updated dropdown lists with entries added via the '+' sign from M2M field.
evidence:
Fix message says: Fixed #36468 -- Fixed failure to close popup when adding a related object in the admin.

The issue manifested when there were multiple relations and only some
of them participated in a filter_horizontal.

Regression in cd0479ff764272add5e0aba2afcf5649a241ca00.
reason: The change added the SelectBox cache update in updateRelatedSelectsOptions without checking that the target select is managed by SelectBox. This throws a JS error that stops the admin popup from closing, and the fix adds exactly that check.
ground_truth: The change added a block to `updateRelatedSelectsOptions` in RelatedObjectLookups.js that, after appending a new option to another related select, calls `SelectBox.add_to_cache(select.id, option)` and `SelectBox.redisplay(select.id)`. The guard is only `window.SelectBox !== undefined && !SelectBox.cache[currentSelect.id]`; it never checks that `select` itself is managed by SelectBox. Consider a form with several relations to the same model where only some use `filter_horizontal`, so SelectBox.js is loaded. Adding an object via the '+' popup then reaches other plain `<select>` widgets that have no `SelectBox.cache` entry. `add_to_cache` then pushes onto an undefined cache entry and throws a TypeError. That aborts `dismissAddRelatedObjectPopup`, so the popup window never closes. The fix adds the condition `SelectBox.cache[select.id]`, so the cache is updated only for fields SelectBox actually manages.

title: Fixed #35782 -- Allowed overriding password validation error messages.
evidence:
Fix message says: Fixed #36314 -- Fixed MinimumLengthValidator error message translation.

Regression in ec7d69035a408b357f1803ca05a7c991cc358cfa.

Thank you Gabriel Trouvé for the report and Claude Paroz for the review.
reason: The change added `get_error_message()` in `MinimumLengthValidator`. That method interpolates `min_length` into the msgids before passing them to `ngettext`, so no catalog lookup matches and translations are lost. This is a behavioral defect, and the fix attributes the regression to this change.
ground_truth: The new `MinimumLengthValidator.get_error_message()` applies `% self.min_length` to each string literal before passing it to `ngettext`. The msgids that `ngettext` receives are therefore already formatted strings, such as "This password is too short. It must contain at least 8 characters.". These never match the translation catalog entries, which contain the `%d` placeholder. As a result, with a non-English active language (e.g. French), the too-short password error is always shown untranslated in English. The fix calls `ngettext` with the unformatted singular/plural msgids and applies `% self.min_length` to the translated result. It also restores `params={"min_length": ...}` on the raised `ValidationError`.

title: Fixed #34619 -- Associated FilteredSelectMultiple elements to their label and help text.
evidence:
Fix message says: Fixed #36423 -- Prevented filter_horizontal buttons from intercepting form submission.

In the admin's filter_horizontal widget, optional action buttons like
"Choose all", "Remove all", etc. were changed from `<a>` to `<button>`
elements in #34619, but without specifying `type="button"`. As a result,
when pressing Enter while focused on a form input, these buttons could
be triggered and intercept form submission.

Explicitly set `type="button"` on these control buttons to prevent them
from acting as submit buttons.

Thanks Antoliny Lee for the quick triage and review.

Regression in 857b1048d53ebf5fc5581c110e85c212b81ca83a.
reason: The change converted the selector controls from <a> links to <button> elements created without type="button". These buttons default to type="submit", so they intercept implicit form submission. This is a behavioral defect visible in the diff.
ground_truth: In `SelectFilter.init` in SelectFilter2.js, the change replaced the "Choose all", "Choose selected", "Remove selected" and "Remove all" `<a>` links with `<button>` elements built via `quickElement('button', ...)`. None of them is given a `type` attribute. Inside a form, a button with no type defaults to `type="submit"`. When a user presses Enter in a text input of an admin change form containing a filter_horizontal/filter_vertical widget, the browser's implicit submission activates the first submit button in tree order. If one of these selector buttons comes first, its click handler fires (moving options, with the event default prevented) instead of the form being saved. The fix adds `'type', 'button'` to all four buttons so they no longer act as submit buttons.

title: Fixed #35936 -- Used unnest for bulk inserts on Postgres when possible.
evidence:
Fix message says: Refs #33647 -- Fixed silent data truncation in bulk_create on Postgres.

Regression in a16eedcf9c69d8a11d94cac1811018c5b996d491.

The UNNEST strategy is affected by the same problem bulk_update has wrt/
to silent data truncation due to its usage of db_type which always returns
a parametrized subtype.
reason: The fix attributes silent data truncation to the UNNEST strategy introduced here, and the faulty line casting to the parametrized `db_type` is added in this change's diff.
ground_truth: The new `SQLInsertCompiler.assemble_as_sql` in the PostgreSQL compiler builds each UNNEST placeholder as `(%s)::<db_type>[]`, where `db_type` comes from `field.db_type(self.connection)`. That type string includes the column's parameters, e.g. `varchar(50)` or `numeric(5, 2)`. In PostgreSQL an explicit cast to a length-limited type silently truncates or rounds values instead of raising an error. So `bulk_create()` of two or more objects whose CharField value exceeds `max_length` silently inserts a truncated string, where the regular VALUES insert would fail with a "value too long" error. The same applies to rounding of decimals. The fix strips the parameters from the type (`db_type.split("(")[0]`), so the cast is to e.g. `varchar[]` and the column's own constraints apply on insert.

title: Fixed CVE-2024-56374 -- Mitigated potential DoS in IPv6 validation.
evidence:
Fix message says: Fixed #36098 -- Fixed validate_ipv6_address()/validate_ipv46_address() crash for non-string values.

Regression in ca2be7724e1244a4cb723de40a070f873c6e94bf.
reason: The change routes `is_valid_ipv6_address()` through the new `_ipv6_address_from_str()`, whose `len()` check crashes on non-string inputs. The fix explicitly blames this change as a regression, and the faulty code is in the diff.
ground_truth: The change makes `is_valid_ipv6_address()` call the new helper `_ipv6_address_from_str()` instead of `ipaddress.IPv6Address(ip_str)`. The helper begins with `if len(ip_str) > max_length`, and `is_valid_ipv6_address()` still only catches `ValueError`. Before, non-string values that `ipaddress.IPv6Address` accepts, such as an `ipaddress.IPv6Address` instance or an int, were handled. Now they raise an uncaught `TypeError` (e.g. "object of type 'IPv6Address' has no len()"). As a result, `validate_ipv6_address(ipaddress.IPv6Address('::1'))` and `validate_ipv46_address(...)` crash instead of validating or raising `ValidationError`. The fix returns True early for `ipaddress.IPv6Address` instances and catches `TypeError` as well as `ValueError`, returning False.

title: Refs #36075 -- Used field in pk_fields over field.primary_key.
evidence:
Fix message says: Refs #36075 -- Adjusted MTI handling of _non_pk_concrete_field_names.

Regression in bf7b17d16d3978b2e1cee4a0f7ce8840bd1a8dc4.

Thanks Sage Abdullah for the report.
reason: In this change, `Options._non_pk_concrete_field_names` now excludes only fields in the model's own `pk_fields`, so inherited parent primary keys under multi-table inheritance are no longer excluded. The fix attributes the regression to this change and restores the exclusion.
ground_truth: The change rewrote `Options._non_pk_concrete_field_names` in options.py to filter with `if field not in self.pk_fields` instead of `if not field.primary_key`. Under multi-table inheritance, a child model's `pk_fields` contains only its own primary key (the parent link). The parent's primary key (e.g. the parent's `id` AutoField) also appears in the child's `concrete_fields` with `primary_key=True`, but it is not in the child's `pk_fields`. As a result, the parent's pk is now reported as an updatable non-pk concrete field. For example, `child.save(update_fields=["id"])` no longer raises the expected ValueError, and code relying on this set, such as the `update_or_create` update_fields subset check, treats the parent pk as a regular field. The fix collects the `pk_fields` of the model and of all its parents (`all_parents`) and excludes all of them. It also updates the save() error message to mention primary keys.

title: Fixed #36116 -- Optimized multi-column ForwardManyToOne prefetching.
evidence:
Fix message says: Fixed #36432 -- Fixed a prefetch_related crash on related target subclass queryset.

Regression in 626d77e52a3f247358514bcf51c761283968099c.

Refs #36116.

Thanks Cornelis Poppema for the excellent report.
reason: The fix names this commit as the regression source. The faulty filter construction, which combines the queryset model's db_table with the raw foreign_related_fields, was added in this diff and causes a crash.
ground_truth: `ForwardManyToOneDescriptor.get_prefetch_querysets()` now filters with `TupleIn(ColPairs(queryset.model._meta.db_table, related_fields, related_fields, self.field), ...)`, where `related_fields = self.field.foreign_related_fields`. Those are fields of the FK's target model, but the table alias comes from the prefetch queryset's model. With a custom prefetch queryset on a multi-table-inheritance subclass of the target, the two do not match. Example: a FK to `Place` prefetched with `Prefetch("place", queryset=Restaurant.objects.all())`. The generated SQL references the parent's column (e.g. `id`) on the child's table, which has no such column, so `prefetch_related` crashes with a database error. The old `field__in` kwarg filter resolved the field names through the ORM and did not have this problem. The fix resolves each field by name against the prefetch queryset (`queryset.query.resolve_ref(field.name).target`), so the columns match the queryset's model.

title: Refs #31170 -- Added JavaScript tests for RelatedObjectLookups.js.
evidence:
Fix message says: Fixed #36284, Refs #31170 -- Ensured related lookup popups are closed properly.

In the admin, when selecting related objects via the helpers defined in
`RelatedObjectLookups.js`, the `dismissRelatedLookupPopup` function was
attempting to access `window.relatedWindows`, which does not exist in
real execution, causing related lookup popups to remain open.
    
This change ensures that this code correctly accesses the module-local
`relatedWindows` by explicitly assigning it to `window.relatedWindows`.
    
Regression in 91bebf1adb43561b54bac18e76224759dc70acb3.
    
Thanks Matthias Kestenholz for the report, the fix ideas, and testing.

Co-authored-by: Matthias Kestenholz <mk@feinheit.ch>
reason: The change rewrote `dismissRelatedLookupPopup` to read the global `window.relatedWindows` instead of the module-local `relatedWindows`. That global is never set in real execution, so the function throws before closing the popup. The fix explicitly calls this a regression from this change.
ground_truth: In `RelatedObjectLookups.js`, the change rewrote `dismissRelatedLookupPopup` to use `window.relatedWindows.indexOf(win)` and `window.relatedWindows.splice(index, 1)` instead of the IIFE-local `relatedWindows` array. The module never assigns `relatedWindows` to `window`, so in a real admin page `window.relatedWindows` is undefined. Calling `.indexOf` on it throws a TypeError before `win.close()` runs. As a result, picking an object in a raw-id/related lookup popup sets the value but leaves the popup open. The new test hid the bug because it created `window.relatedWindows` itself. The fix went back to the module-local `relatedWindows`, exported it as `window.relatedWindows = relatedWindows`, and removed the test's own initialization.

title: Fixed CVE-2025-26699 -- Mitigated potential DoS in wordwrap template filter.
evidence:
Fix message says: Fixed #36341 -- Preserved whitespaces in wordwrap template filter.

Regression in 55d89e25f4115c5674cdd9b9bcba2bb2bb6d820b.

This work improves the django.utils.text.wrap() function to ensure that
empty lines and lines with whitespace only are kept instead of being
dropped.

Thanks Matti Pohjanvirta for the report and fix.

Co-authored-by: Natalia <124304+nessita@users.noreply.github.com>
reason: The fix names this change as the source of the regression, and the faulty rewrite of `wrap()` is right there in the diff: empty and whitespace-only lines get dropped, and trailing newlines are lost.
ground_truth:
The rewritten `django.utils.text.wrap()` loops over `text.splitlines(True)`, passes each line to `textwrap.TextWrapper.wrap()`, and joins the pieces with "
". `TextWrapper.wrap()` returns an empty list for an empty or whitespace-only line, so those lines vanish from the output. With the default `replace_whitespace=True`, the trailing newline kept by `splitlines(True)` becomes a space and is dropped, so a trailing newline in the input is lost too. For example, `wordwrap("first

second
", 80)` returns "first
second" instead of "first

second
", which merges paragraphs in templates. The fix sets `replace_whitespace=False` and splits with `splitlines()` (no kept ends). It appends the original line whenever the wrapper returns nothing, and appends a final empty element when the text ends with "
".

title: Fixed #36217 -- Restored pre_save/post_save signal emission via LogEntry.save() for single-object deletion in the admin.
evidence:
Fix message says: Fixed #36234 -- Restored single_object argument to LogEntry.objects.log_actions().

Thank you Adam Johnson for the report and fix. Thank you Sarah Boyce for
your spot on analysis.

Regression in c09bceef68e5abb79accedd12dade16aa6577a09, which is
partially reverted in this branch.

Co-authored-by: Sarah Boyce <42296566+sarahboyce@users.noreply.github.com>
reason: The fix attributes the regression to this change and partially reverts it. The change visibly removed a public keyword argument and changed the return type of `log_actions()` for one-element querysets, which breaks the API contract.
ground_truth: The change removed the keyword-only `single_object` parameter from `LogEntryManager.log_actions()` and replaced the `if single_object and log_entry_list` check with `if len(log_entry_list) == 1`, which returns the bare saved instance. This breaks the public API released in Django 5.1 in two ways. First, third-party code calling `LogEntry.objects.log_actions(..., single_object=True)` now fails with `TypeError: unexpected keyword argument 'single_object'` after a point-release upgrade. Second, callers passing a multi-object queryset that happens to contain exactly one object now get a single `LogEntry` instance instead of a list, so code that iterates or indexes the result breaks. The fix restores the `single_object=False` keyword argument and passes it from `log_addition`/`log_change`. It keeps saving one-element lists via `save()` so signals still fire, but returns `[instance]` unless `single_object` is true.

title: Fixed #27222 -- Refreshed model field values assigned expressions on save().
evidence:
Fix message says: Refs #27222 -- Restored Model.save()'s refreshing of db_returning fields even if a value is set.

The logic could likely be adjusted to assign the pre_save value in most cases
to avoid the database transit but it could break in subtle ways so it's not
worth the complexity it would require.

Regression in 94680437a45a71c70ca8bd2e68b72aa1e2eff337.

Co-authored-by: Tim Graham <timograham@gmail.com>
reason: The fix names this change as the regression. The change added code to the insert path of `Model._save_table` that drops `db_returning` fields from `returning_fields` when they have a concrete value, so those fields are no longer refreshed from the database: a behavioral defect visible in the diff.
ground_truth: In the insert branch of `Model._save_table`, the change builds `returning_fields = list(meta.db_returning_fields)` and then, for each insert field, calls `returning_fields.remove(field)` (the `elif field.db_returning:` branch) whenever the field's pre_save value is not an expression. Before this change, every `db_returning` field was always fetched back via RETURNING and assigned to the instance. Now a `db_returning` field with an explicitly set value keeps the in-memory Python value instead of the value the database actually stored. This happens even on backends that support RETURNING (PostgreSQL, SQLite, Oracle). For example, an explicitly set primary key or a custom `db_returning=True` field whose stored or converted value (via `from_db_value`, normalization or triggers) differs from the assigned value is left stale on the instance after `save()`/`create()`. The fix only removes such fields from `returning_fields` when the backend cannot return columns from insert, and never removes the auto field when the pk was set.

title: Fixed #34917 -- Underlined links in the main content area of the admin.
evidence:
Fix message says: Fixed #36528, Refs #34917 -- Removed role="button" from object-tools links.

Regression in 849f8307a5bb33465252d0891a9b2c47dde65889.
In order to prevent underlines on links styled like buttons, role="button" was added.
This has been removed and the style updated to reflect that these are links.
reason: The blamed defect is an accessibility and semantics issue: `role="button"` was added to object-tools navigation links purely to avoid an underline style. It is presentation/markup, not a functional runtime defect such as a wrong result, crash or data loss.

title: Refs #34619 -- Fixed labels width in FilteredSelectMultiple in the admin.
evidence:
Fix message says: Fixed #36601 -- Fixed color contrast of FilteredSelectMultiple widget chosen labels in TabularInlines.

Regression in a0f50c2a483678d31bd1ad6f08fd3a0b8399e27b.
reason: The defect is a CSS-only visual issue: the label color contrast is wrong in TabularInlines because of selector scoping, with no behavioral effect.

title: Fixed #36289 -- Fixed bulk_create() crash with nullable geometry fields on PostGIS.
evidence:
Fix message says: Fixed #36502 -- Restored UNNEST strategy for foreign key bulk inserts on PostgreSQL.

Regression in 764af7a3d6c0b543dcf659a2c327f214da768fe4.
reason: The new `get_internal_type()` check returns "ForeignKey" for relation fields, which only makes FK bulk inserts fall back from the UNNEST optimization to the standard VALUES insert; results stay correct, so this is a performance-only regression, not a behavioral defect.

title: Fixed #36273 -- Moved Index system checks from Model to Index.check().
evidence:
Fix message says: Fixed #36660 -- Fixed a regression in descending Index local field checks.

Regression in 8638d8bf74c1a58302c97d4436ad2eb08438145b.

Refs #36273.

Thanks Federico Bond for the report.
reason: The fix explicitly names this change as the regression. The faulty `{*self.fields, ...}` call to `_check_local_fields` is added in this diff, and it causes spurious check errors for valid models.
ground_truth: The new `Index.check()` method passes `{*self.fields, *self.include, *references}` to `model._check_local_fields()`. `self.fields` holds the raw field strings, including the "-" prefix used for descending order. The old Model-level check used the field names from `index.fields_orders`, which has that prefix stripped. As a result, a valid index such as `models.Index(fields=["-name"], name="idx")` now fails the system check with "'indexes' refers to the nonexistent field '-name'" (models.E012). The fix passes `field for field, _ in self.fields_orders` instead of `self.fields`.

title: Fixed #27489 -- Renamed permissions upon model renaming in migrations.
evidence:
Fix message says: Refs #27489 -- Made RenamePermission() operation respect database.

Regression in f02b49d2f3bf84f5225de920ca510149f1f9f1da.

Co-authored-by: Mariusz Felisiak <felisiak.mariusz@gmail.com>
reason: The fix names this change as the source of the regression. The faulty queries in `RenamePermission._rename` were added in this diff. The bug is behavioral: permissions are queried and renamed on the wrong database when migrating a non-default database.
ground_truth: In the new `RenamePermission._rename`, the code reads `db = schema_editor.connection.alias` but never applies it to the lookups. `ContentType.objects.filter(...)` and `Permission.objects.filter(content_type_id__in=...)` therefore run against the default (router-chosen) database rather than the one being migrated. Running `migrate --database=other` on an app with a `RenameModel` reads and renames permissions in the default database, or finds nothing there. Meanwhile the permissions in the database actually being migrated keep their old codenames and names. The fix adds `.using(db)` to both the ContentType and Permission querysets so the operation works on the migration's database connection.

title: Fixed #36366 -- Improved accessibility of pagination in the admin.
evidence:
Fix message says: Fixed #36558, Refs #36366 -- Fixed the "show all" link hover styling in admin pagination.

Regression in 3f59711581bd22ebd0f13fb040b15b69c0eee21f.
reason: The bug is a CSS-only hover styling regression on the "Show all" link, which is visual and not a behavioral defect.

title: Fixed #36210, Refs #36181 -- Allowed Subquery usage in further lookups against composite pks.
evidence:
Fix message says: Refs #36210 -- Corrected output_field comparison in Subquery.resolve_expression().

Regression in fd569dd45bf0746378faf7f65172497f21ed27f0.
reason: The fix explicitly marks this change as the regression. It corrects the output_field comparison that this change added in Subquery.resolve_expression(), which made the shim-removal logic misbehave.
ground_truth: The new `Subquery.resolve_expression()` is meant to drop the Subquery shim and return the bare resolved `Query`. It is supposed to wrap the query in an `ExpressionWrapper` only when the user passed an `output_field` that differs from the query's own. It tests this with `self.output_field != resolved.query.output_field`, but `Field.__eq__` compares fields by `creation_counter` and model, not by kind. So a separately instantiated field such as `IntegerField()` never equals the query's model field. As a result, any `Subquery(..., output_field=X())` is always wrapped in an `ExpressionWrapper`, even when `X` is the same field type as the selected column. Lookups that introspect the right-hand side as a `Query` then no longer recognize it, defeating the purpose of the change. One example is the tuple lookups' `isinstance(self.rhs, Query)` check, which is supposed to raise `NotSupportedError` for composite-pk comparisons against subqueries. The fix compares field types (`type(self.output_field) is not type(resolved.query.output_field)`) instead of using field equality.

title: Fixed #34041 -- Added aria-current attribute to admin breadcrumbs.
evidence:
Fix message says: Fixed #37378 -- Removed extra empty breadcrumb in admindocs model index.

Regression in bc03f1064e10fa247a46d4e8a98ba9b26aa4790d.

reason: A typo in the rewritten admindocs model index breadcrumb, added by this change, makes the template render an extra empty `<li>` in the breadcrumb list. The fix attributes the regression to this change and corrects that exact line.
ground_truth:
In `admin_doc/model_index.html`, the new breadcrumb markup closes the 'Documentation' item with `
  • ` instead of `
    • `: `
  • Documentation
  • `. The HTML parser treats this as the start of a new list item. So the admindocs Models index page renders a spurious empty `
  • ` between 'Documentation' and 'Models'. The empty item gets the CSS separator from `li:not([aria-current="page"])::after`, so the page shows a doubled '›' and assistive technology announces an extra empty breadcrumb item. The fix replaces the stray `
  • ` with the closing `
    • ` tag.

title: Fixed writer_name deprecation warning in docutils 0.22+.
evidence:
Fix message says: Fixed #36535 -- Ensured compatibility with docutils 0.19 through 0.22.

Regression in 65ab92f6a83644bbb555d0eff3a02d8d9301aba4.
reason: The change swapped `writer_name="html"` for `writer="html"` in `parse_rst`. On docutils older than 0.22 that string is not accepted and parsing breaks, and the fix explicitly blames this change as a regression.
ground_truth: In `django/contrib/admindocs/utils.py`, `parse_rst()` was changed to call `docutils.core.publish_parts(..., writer="html", ...)` instead of `writer_name="html"`, to silence a deprecation warning in docutils 0.22+. Passing a string writer name through the `writer` parameter only works in docutils 0.22+. In docutils 0.19–0.21, `writer` must be a writer instance. With an older docutils installed, every admindocs reStructuredText rendering (docstrings for views, models, template tags, filters) therefore fails, typically with an AttributeError when docutils treats the string "html" as a writer object. The fix creates an instance with `docutils.writers.get_writer_class("html")()` and passes that as `writer`, which works across docutils 0.19 through 0.22.

title: Fixed #36727 -- Deprecated Field.get_placeholder in favor of get_placeholder_sql.
evidence:
Fix message says: Fixed #37322 -- Avoided transforms on spatial fields with srid=None.

After adjusting spatial queries to no longer interpolate the SRID param
into the SQL template, an "srid=None" attribute on a spatial field became
a valid input to the ST_Transform() function on PostGIS & SpatiaLite,
returning NULL for the entire value. (Before, the string "None" was
interpolated into the SQL, which crashed.)

srid=-1 is the documented way to express an undefined SRID, but it's
possible that users could experiment with unmanaged models with srid=None:
those uses should raise errors instead of silently persisting NULL.

Thanks Natalia Bidart for advice.

Regression in 1a8fd5cf75bf855852f6bc2f75c3da9f7b145669.

Co-authored-by: Jacob Walls <jacobtylerwalls@gmail.com>
reason: This change moved the target SRID from an interpolated SQL string to a query parameter. A field with srid=None now produces ST_Transform(geom, NULL), which silently stores or compares NULL where it used to raise an SQL error; the fix attributes the regression to this change.
ground_truth: The rewritten `get_geom_placeholder_sql` in `BaseSpatialOperations` and `PostGISOperations` now passes the field's SRID as a query parameter (`params = (*params, f.srid)` / `(value, f.srid)`) instead of interpolating it into the SQL. Before, a spatial field with `srid=None` produced SQL like `ST_Transform(%s, None)`, which failed loudly. Now `None` is bound as SQL NULL, and the transform check (`value.srid != field.srid`) is true for any geometry with a real SRID. So the database runs `ST_Transform(geom, NULL)`, which returns NULL on PostGIS/SpatiaLite. For example, saving `Point(1, 2, srid=4326)` to a geometry field declared with `srid=None` (e.g. on an unmanaged model) silently stores NULL instead of the geometry, which is data loss; lookups against such fields are similarly broken. The fix makes the must-transform check raise `ValueError("Cannot transform a spatial value to an undefined SRID.")` when the field SRID is None, and makes the PostGIS backend use that shared check.

title: Fixed #36865 -- Removed casting from exact lookups in admin searches.
evidence:
Fix message says: Fixed #37263 -- Fixed changelist __exact search crashes and over-matching.

Search terms for non-text `__exact` `search_fields` entries were validated
with the model field's `formfield().to_python()`, which failed to reject
invalid terms for two kinds of fields:

- Fields with choices use `TypedChoiceField`, whose `to_python()` returns
  the raw string unvalidated, so any non-matching search term (e.g.
  `"john"` against an `IntegerField` with `choices`) reached the ORM and
  crashed the changelist with a `ValueError` (HTTP 500).

- `BooleanField` uses `forms.BooleanField`, whose `to_python()` maps almost
  any string to `True`, so an arbitrary search term OR-matched every row
  with a `True` value instead of matching nothing.

Boolean search terms are now parsed such that arbitrary strings do not
match anything, and Typed(Multiple)ChoiceField search terms now coerce
to the correct types.

Regression in 4cecf3039586ea738afafb9a28c946bff42c37c1.

Thanks Adam Johnson for the report and Sarah Boyce for the review.

Co-authored-by: Jacob Walls <jacobtylerwalls@gmail.com>
reason: The fix explicitly names this change as the regression source. The faulty validation code, which calls `validate_field.formfield().to_python(bit)` inside `get_search_results`, is added in this diff and causes crashes and wrong results.
ground_truth: The change rewrote `ModelAdmin.get_search_results` so that, for non-text `__exact` search fields, each search term is validated with `validate_field.formfield().to_python(bit)`. Lookups whose term raises `ValidationError` are skipped; all others are passed to the ORM with the converted value. This validation does not reject invalid terms for two kinds of fields. First, fields with `choices` produce a `TypedChoiceField`, whose `to_python()` returns the raw string unchanged. So searching "john" against an `IntegerField(choices=...)` with `field__exact` sends "john" to the ORM, which raises `ValueError` and makes the changelist return HTTP 500. Second, `forms.BooleanField.to_python()` maps almost any non-false string to True, so an arbitrary term like "xyz" against `bool__exact` matches every row where the field is True instead of matching nothing. The fix uses `formfield.clean()` for Typed(Multiple)ChoiceField so values are coerced and validated, and uses strict boolean and null-boolean parsers that raise `ValidationError` for unrecognized strings.

title: Fixed #36926 -- Made admin use boolean icons for related BooleanFields in list_display.
evidence:
Fix message says: Fixed #37230 -- Fixed a crash for second-degree relations in ModelAdmin.list_display.

Thanks Rob Kuipers for the report.

Regression in 4b2b4bf0ac2707dc9c4d51cabfa72168eaea95fe.

Co-authored-by: Jacob Walls <jacobtylerwalls@gmail.com>
reason: The fix explicitly calls this change a regression and removes the `get_fields_from_path` call it added to `lookup_field`. That code is plainly in this diff and causes a crash, which is a behavioral defect.
ground_truth: The change makes `lookup_field()` in `django/contrib/admin/utils.py` call `get_fields_from_path(opts.model, name)[-1]` unconditionally whenever a `list_display` name contains `__`, so it can render boolean icons for related BooleanFields. Before this, such names were resolved only by walking attributes with `getattr`, which also works for paths whose last part is not a concrete model field, such as a method, a property or `__str__` on a related model. `get_fields_from_path` raises `FieldDoesNotExist` for those paths, and the exception is not caught. Because `lookup_field` is shared by the changelist and readonly-field rendering, entries traversing relations, including second-degree ones (e.g. `book__author__get_full_name` or `parent__parent__some_property`), now crash with an exception where they previously displayed fine. The fix removes this lookup from `lookup_field`. It instead resolves the final field only in `items_for_result` when `f` is None, wrapped in `try/except FieldDoesNotExist`.

title: Fixed #35738 -- Deprecated double-dot variable lookups.
evidence:
Fix message says: Fixed #37257, Refs #35738 -- Prevented double-dot deprecation warnings for template literals.

The deprecation warning for double-dot variable lookups checked
str(filter_expression.var), which for constants is the resolved literal
value rather than a variable lookup. Templates containing string or translated
string literals with two consecutive dots, such as {{ "a..b" }} or
{{ 'a..b'|upper }}, therefore incorrectly raised a RemovedInDjango70Warning.

The check now only applies when the filter expression's variable is a
Variable lookup.

Regression in 5d911f2d2fecc703be91b2b9b28acc59d34b35f3.
reason: The change added a double-dot check that also fires on string literals, and the fix corrects exactly that line. This is a behavioral defect: spurious warnings, which break rendering under -Werror.
ground_truth: The new deprecation check in `Parser.parse()` for variable nodes tests `".." in str(filter_expression.var)`. For constant expressions, `filter_expression.var` is the resolved literal value (a string or translated string), not a `Variable` lookup. So a template containing a literal with two consecutive dots, such as `{{ "a..b" }}` or `{{ 'a..b'|upper }}`, wrongly emits a `RemovedInDjango70Warning` about double-dot lookups. That warning becomes an exception when warnings are treated as errors. The check would also reject valid templates once it is elevated to an error as planned. The fix applies the check only when the expression is a variable lookup: `filter_expression.is_var and ".." in filter_expression.var.var`.
